messages:
Anya Park: Heads up — customer reported a sudden drop in embeddings throughput for /v1/embeddings this morning. Tokens/sec looks stable on their side, but vectors/sec is down ~40% vs yesterday. They say latency per request is only slightly up, but the service is returning fewer vectors/sec overall (they batch 64 inputs per request).

Anya Park: Quick context: model=embed-large-v1-quant, region=us-west, dedicated pool, autoscale on. No model rollouts in the last 24h from our side AFAIK.

Sam (Support): @Anya pulled logs from their account (redwood-corp-987). Posting the tail of the worker logs around the drop window: 
```
[2028-09-15T09:12:18Z] INFO batcher: accepting batch size=64, queue_latency_ms=12
[2028-09-15T09:12:18Z] WARN gpu-scheduler: queued_batches=35, inflight_batches=2
[2028-09-15T09:12:19Z] INFO runtime: tokens_processed=124567, vectors_emitted=4096
[2028-09-15T09:12:19Z] WARN kvcache: miss_rate=0.02
[2028-09-15T09:12:20Z] INFO runtime: tokens_processed=125003, vectors_emitted=2560
[2028-09-15T09:12:20Z] ERROR runtimeserv: batch_drop: reason=timeout threshold_ms=1500
```

Sam (Support): They also included a sample job that used to yield ~1500 vectors/sec but is now ~900 vectors/sec.

James Li: Thanks. Initial read: high queued_batches + low inflight suggests the scheduler can't push work to GPUs fast enough — likely contention at the execution layer (kernel scheduling / memory pressure) rather than network.

James Li: Can @morgan share GPU util / mem & queue depth from that time window? Also need to verify quantized variant behavior: sometimes quantized kernels reduce vector throughput under certain sequence-length distributions.

ops-bot: metric alert: embeddings_vectors/s rolling 5m dropped 42% for customer redwood-corp-987 at 2028-09-15T09:11:00Z.

Morgan Chen: Pushing the cluster metrics. Snapshot around 09:12: 
```
node-23.gpu: util=95%, mem_used=38.2GB/40GB, gpu_temp=81C
node-25.gpu: util=48%, mem_used=20.1GB/40GB, gpu_temp=70C
queue-metrics: global_queue_depth=420, avg_batch_size=34, max_wait_ms=1900
kernel-waits: avg_kernel_launch_delay_ms=12.5
```

Morgan Chen: Interesting: one node is saturated (node-23) while others are underutilized — looks like skewed routing. That would explain tokens/sec staying steady (requests accepted) but vectors/sec lower because big backlog + some batches being dropped/timeout.

Eli (QA): Repro attempt on staging: I ran a 10 minute load with identical batch-size=64 payloads against embed-large-v1-quant. Numbers:
```
staging run A: steady tokens/s ~ 12.1k, vectors/s ~ 1.6k
staging run B (with concurrency=8): tokens/s ~12.0k, vectors/s ~1.0k, queue_depth spike to 300
```

Eli (QA): When I forced routing to the non-quant variant (embed-large-v1), vectors/s returned to ~1.7k and queue depth normalized. So quant variant + concurrency seems correlated.

James Li: That points to a routing/pool-assignment change or autoscaler edge case that is overpacking node-23 with quantized workloads. Maybe bin-packing changed after a recent scheduler tweak.

Anya Park: Customer also attached their request examples: they send JSON array of 64 short texts (avg 18 tokens). Their client uses our SDK which sets `max_batch_size=64` and `concurrency=16`.

Sam (Support): Repro steps for eng to validate locally:
1) curl the embeddings endpoint with 64 short items.
2) set concurrency=16 in client.
3) target embed-large-v1-quant and compare to embed-large-v1.

Sam (Support): Example curl: 
```bash
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": ["s1","s2",... repeated 64 times]}' \
  https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings?model=embed-large-v1-quant
```

James Li: Quick mitigation while we investigate: 1) temporarily lower default concurrency for quant pools to 8 via feature flag; 2) add routing weight to spread quant workloads to nodes with available mem; 3) backout the recent scheduler bin-packing change if we see immediate regression.

Morgan Chen: I can push a routing tweak to shift some shards off node-23. Rolling change will take ~2 mins and should drop queue depth.

Eli (QA): I also saw a handful of `batch_drop: reason=timeout` in logs — can we increase the batch timeout threshold to avoid dropping in transient backpressure? Pros/cons: prevents small loss but may increase latency.

James Li: Agree — short-term raise timeout by 500ms for that pool. We'll monitor latency SLOs. If vectors/sec recovers, plan to revert scheduler change and run a canary.

billing-bot: note: customer redwood-corp-987 is on Dedicated Tier B with reserved capacity. No billing throttles detected.

Anya Park: I'll tell the customer we have a mitigation in progress (routing + longer batch timeout) and ask them to hold off any config changes. @James @Morgan any ETA for a fix?

Morgan Chen: Routing change in 5m, batch-timeout bump deployed in 10m. Will post metrics after.

ops-bot: action: create incident CR-987-embed-throughput (priority=P2) assigned to eng-runtime, infra.

Eli (QA): Post-change staging repro: with routing change and timeout bump, quant variant vectors/s improved to ~1.5k and queue_depth dropped to ~90. Not fully back to non-quant, but much better.

James Li: Next steps: 1) run scheduler bin-packing revert in canary, 2) add metric alert on node-skew (if one node >80% util and others <60% for 1m), 3) capture kernel-level telemetry for quant kernels to see stalls.

Anya Park: Cool. I'll update the customer with a summary + ETA and ask for any additional repro logs. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Morgan Chen: Posting follow-up metric after routing change (09:20): global_queue_depth=78, avg_batch_size=45, node-23.util=72% — looks stable.

Sam (Support): Customer reply: "saw immediate improvement, still slightly lower than baseline but acceptable for now. Thanks for the fast help!" :relieved:

James Li: Marking this as monitored. We'll keep incident open until we finish scheduler revert & kernel traces.

ops-bot: incident CR-987-embed-throughput status=investigating, created_by=Sam (Support)

Anya Park: Closing loop: action items assigned in the incident. I'll paste the incident link in the ticket.

Eli (QA): Note for postmortem: include sample client payloads, concurrency patterns, and comparison of quant vs non-quant kernel latencies.

James Li: Good call. If anyone sees a recurrence ping this thread.
